thread:
Lina: Quick thread: proposing a compact v2 pin metadata shape that unifies visibility, TTL intent, and precedence. Goal is small wire format for routing but clear operational semantics for Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Thoughts?
Jared: +1. One thing we should call out: "soft" TTL should mark a pin as "degradable" not immediately removable. Soft -> deprioritize in router; hard -> forbid selection.
Priya: Agree. Suggest names: vis (global|tenant|ephemeral), s_t (soft ttl seconds), h_t (hard ttl seconds), pr (precedence hint), o (origin). Keep keys 1-3 chars.
Vik: Important: precedence must be deterministic across merges: tenant_override > tenant_pin > org_pin > global. Also add a field "merge_strategy": "prefer_higher_precedence" to avoid client ambiguity.
Lina: For wire size, maybe encode precedence as numeric (0 default, 10 tenant_override, etc.). We'll map in console.
Jared: Also need a "grace_seconds" so that when hard_ttl elapses we give a short window for traffic draining and rollback probes. E.g., h_t + grace = eviction time.
Priya: For private/on-prem, can't rely on central migration. We need local-agent compatibility: add header `X-Pin-Schema: v2` and servers must accept absent fields as v1. Backpressure: older clients might not send v2 header so server defaults to legacy semantics.
Vik: Telemetry: increment counters on s_t->h_t transitions, and tag by origin & visibility. Add histogram for time-between-soft-and-hard to detect delayed GC.
ops-bot: deploybot: rolling flag set for pin-schema-v2: canary at 2026-04-05T04:00Z. Will emit `Warning:pin-schema-deprecated` for legacy flows during canary.
Lina: Migration plan: 1) dry-run backfill that computes numeric precedence for existing rows, 2) experiment with marking a subset of tenant pins as vis=tenant and s_t/h_t populated, 3) run telemetry checks for regressions.
Jared: SDK note: older SDKs ignore unknown keys but may not honor s_t/h_t semantics when probing. Need server-side enforcement (i.e., server decides selection regardless of client). Also add a boolean "probe_ok" to indicate safe pings from clients won't trigger eviction side-effects.
Priya: Example compact doc for discussion:
```
{ "v":2, "vis":"tenant", "s_t":3600, "h_t":7200, "g":300, "pr":20, "o":"auto", "ver":"b7c1d2", "probe_ok":true }
```
Vik: Suggest change: rename `g` -> `grace` or `g_secs` for clarity in logs. But ok if we keep super-compact on the wire. Console expands names.
Lina: Other cross-cutting: routing layer must support `prefer_fresh` policy to avoid serving soft-expired pins unless explicitly allowed. We should add a route-level override flag.
Jared: Security: for Private, origin field must be signed by the control plane or local admin to prevent tampering. Add a tiny "sig" field (base64) for verification in Private deployments.
Priya: Action items: Lina to write RFC PR with compact JSON + explanations, Vik to draft migration dry-run SQL and verify performance on large pin table, Jared to add server-side enforcement tests and SDK note, ops-bot will run canary.
Lina: Cool. I'll also include backward-compat checklist: server default = legacy behavior if v missing; header `X-Pin-Schema` opt-in for v2; telemetry tags for every TTL event.
Vik: One more: recommend recording `created_by` and `created_at` in control-plane store (verbose fields) but not on the wire. Console can fetch them for debugging.
Jared: Nits: use ISO8601 for console-visible timestamps; wire uses epoch seconds.
Lina: Thanks all. I'll open PR and tag y'all. :sparkles:
__notes: Slack thread discussing a compact v2 pin/rollout metadata shape: visibility, soft/hard TTL semantics, precedence, migration plan, telemetry and compatibility headers. Includes compact JSON example and action items.
